caption: Most planning fails when every task feels urgent. This carousel gives five compact prompts to fix that, step by step. Which task will you re-prioritize first this week? #AIforProductivity #StartupLife #ProductivityHacks #Entrepreneur

slides.title: Stop treating every task urgent.
slides.body: Problem: you treat every task as urgent; this weak approach wastes time. Here are five prompts to fix prioritization.

slides.title: 1. Diagnose method
slides.body: Prompt: Analyze my weekly task list; identify why prioritization fails. Input: [tasks]; Output: 1-3 concrete failure patterns.

slides.title: 2. Improve with impact/effort
slides.body: Prompt: Create an impact/effort matrix for [tasks]; label each as high/low impact and easy/difficult; output top 3 priorities.

slides.title: 3. Apply timeboxing
slides.body: Prompt: For the next 2 days, block time for [top priorities]; output schedule with 2-hour blocks and buffer.

slides.title: 4. Check constraints
slides.body: Prompt: Compare [tasks] against deadlines, capacity, and energy; output red-yellow-green readiness for each.

slides.title: 5. Refine into a rubric
slides.body: Prompt: Turn prioritization criteria into a 5-point rubric; output a scoring sheet and example for [task].

slides.title: Takeaway
slides.body: Adopt a single, repeatable prioritization method so you decide fast and finish more high-impact tasks.
